title: Common Ground restoration campaign
audience: Local residents considering volunteering or donating to watershed restoration
scenario: Common Ground is recruiting volunteers for a six-month river restoration campaign across three neighborhoods.
task: Build an editorial campaign page that explains the work, makes participation feel concrete, and supports both volunteering and donations.

content.primary_heading: A living river starts on its banks
sections: Navigation with The project, Field days, Our impact, About, Donate, and Join a field day
Hero with campaign statement, Join a field day, and Explore the project
Project explanation covering invasive removal, native planting, and water monitoring
Upcoming field days in Riverside on May 9, Eastbank on May 23, and Mill Creek on June 6
Impact facts: 3 neighborhoods, 18 river acres, and 6 months of field work
Volunteer testimonial from Sam Ortiz, Riverside resident
Donation and newsletter calls to action with footer

requirements: Present each field day with place, date, activity, and a clear signup action
Keep volunteer participation primary while preserving a distinct donate path
Explain what a first-time volunteer should expect
Use time elements or equivalently machine-readable dates
Provide useful alternative text for any content-bearing environmental imagery
constraints: Do not use guilt-based, catastrophic, or unverifiable impact language
Do not add donation amounts or tax claims
Do not use remote media or map embeds
Do not hide event details behind interaction
evaluation_focus: Warm civic tone without sacrificing logistical clarity
Scannable event information and action hierarchy
